column2: Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization; Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels
column3: I mapped Authentication to Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization and Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels because credentials and API keys are validated by the authentication layer and are used to establish authorized identity-based access.
column4: Reuse standard session/API-key concepts and implement configurable HoneyPrint credentials and access behavior. (Python (aiohttp-session + cryptography + secrets + hmac + PyYAML))
column5: Control access while supporting believable valid, weak, failed, and session-based authentication scenarios.
column6: Authentication/session state plus structured success/failure events for later analysis.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped Command Handler to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it routes high-level management actions as well as low-level firmware commands to the appropriate execution path.
column4: Build a shared HoneyPrint API/command routing layer that forwards management and firmware actions to the correct emulator functions. (Python (aiohttp + asyncio + re + dict-based dispatch))
column5: Normalize incoming management actions and commands before they update firmware or printer state.
column6: Validated actions routed to file, job, state, or firmware handlers with source/channel context.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped State Management to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it maintains the job, device, and session state that must remain consistent across management controls and firmware behavior.
column4: Build/extend shared HoneyPrint session, job, and printer-state objects used across interfaces. (Python (asyncio + dataclasses + enum))
column5: Keep web, API, Telnet, firmware, and telemetry views synchronized around one coherent runtime state.
column6: Consistent session, job, device, and interaction state available to all active interfaces.

column2: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network
column3: I mapped File Management to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network because it stores G-code job files locally and manages their upload, selection, and transfer into the printer workflow.
column4: Extend HoneyPrint virtual storage using normal asynchronous file operations and metadata handling. (Python (pathlib + aiofiles + mimetypes + hashlib))
column5: Support listing, upload, download, deletion, selection, and persistence of G-code/configuration artifacts.
column6: Updated virtual file inventory plus persistent attacker-supplied files and associated metadata.

column2: Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization; Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels
column3: I mapped Session Control to Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization and Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels because authenticated sessions preserve the identity and access context established after successful login.
column4: Reuse session concepts and extend HoneyPrint session lifecycle logic. (Python (aiohttp-session + secrets + datetime))
column5: Maintain believable authenticated and unauthenticated interaction state across management actions.
column6: Session creation, expiry, logout, and authenticated-access state shared by relevant host services.

column3: I marked Host Configuration as having no direct AM Process Flow counterpart because it configures HoneyPrint deployment parameters such as ports, credentials, and printer personality rather than representing a manufacturing-process function.
column4: Reuse YAML/environment configuration and maintain a custom HoneyPrint configuration schema. (Python (PyYAML + pydantic + python-dotenv + os.environ))
column5: Control credentials, ports, service exposure, printer personality, and host-side runtime settings without code changes.
column6: Declarative deployment configuration that changes the exposed host personality and access conditions.

column2: Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network; Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links
column3: I mapped Network Simulation to Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network and Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links because it models communication effects such as latency, jitter, packet loss, and availability on the printer's operational network connections.
column4: Extend the custom HoneyPrint NetworkSimulator for configurable latency, jitter, loss, and availability behavior. (Python (asyncio + random + time + collections.deque))
column5: Model imperfect printer-network conditions instead of deterministic zero-delay communication.
column6: Configurable delay, loss, and availability decisions that can be applied to host-facing traffic.

column3: I mapped Access Evidence to Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it captures authentication, API, file, and Telnet activity as structured records for later reconstruction and analysis.
column4: Normalize authentication, API, file, and Telnet activity into the shared HoneyPrint evidence pipeline. (Python (asyncio.Queue + logging + dataclasses + uuid))
column5: Preserve host-domain actions with enough context for later cross-stage reconstruction.
column6: Correlated access events with session/source/channel context ready for Stage 5 storage and analysis.
